machine: Apple M4, 10 cores, 32 GiB unified memory, macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)
note: All generators produce bit-identical output; see verify.py and the cmp checks in the write-up. Times are single-threaded wall clock. Generation is Theta(N^2) in cell updates, /64 by bit packing.

variants.gen30.c: scalar, in-place, descending word walk (one row buffer)
variants.gen30v4.c: NEON 128-bit, in-place, descending, 4x unrolled -- FASTEST, used for the long run

findings: Double-buffering (v2) is 2.3x SLOWER at N=1e6 than in-place: the extra write stream costs more than the removed loop-carried dependence buys.
Plain NEON (v3) is a wash vs scalar (77.3s vs 75.4s at N=3e6); the scalar loop was already issue-bound, not width-bound.
NEON + 4x unroll (v4) gives 1.17x over scalar (64.2s vs 75.4s at N=3e6). That is the whole vectorization payoff; the kernel is load/store-port bound.
Measured steady-state throughput ~1.9e9 64-bit word updates/sec/core, i.e. ~1.2e11 cell updates/sec/core.

cost_model.form: T(N) = N^2 / (2K) seconds, K = (instantaneous steps/sec) * t
cost_model.K_note: K is NOT constant: it falls steadily as the row outgrows cache. The pure N^2 model with a fixed K underestimates cost.
cost_model.measured_local_exponent_note: T ~ N^2.4 over 3e6..8e6 (cache transition), vs the asymptotic N^2.0 of the work itself. Expect relaxation toward 2.0 once fully bandwidth-bound.

projected_wall_clock_single_core.1e9: ~145 days at exponent 2.0 from the 8e6 anchor

memory_bandwidth_floor.total_bytes_touched: N^2/4 (in-place: read+write the whole row every step)
memory_bandwidth_floor.single_core_bandwidth_note: A single core cannot saturate 120 GB/s; at a realistic 40 GB/s the single-core bandwidth floor alone is ~72 days for N=1e9, consistent with the ~145-day compute projection.
memory_bandwidth_floor.meaning: Even with perfect use of all 10 cores, this machine cannot reach 1e9 in under ~24 days. Multicore does not rescue 1e9 locally.
